messages:
Maria: kicking off a quick thread with results from the KV cache hybrid prefetch/evict runs across regions. goal: understand hitrate vs p99 tradeoffs for different seqlen mixes.
Ajay: sweet, what traces did you use?
Maria: 10k convo sample (prod-synth) w/ seqlen distribution: 60% <512, 32% 512-1024, 8% >1024. Ran on us-east (H100) and eu-west (A100) with identical orchestration.
Kevin: short summary numbers pls.
Maria: hitrate / token-p99 (single-token p99 observed at request time). no-prefetch: hitrate 0.64, p99(us-east)=85ms, p99(eu-west)=120ms. static-prefetch p=0.3: hitrate 0.71, p99(us-east)=92ms, p99(eu-west)=145ms. static p=0.6: hitrate 0.74, p99(us-east)=110ms, p99(eu-west)=170ms.
Lisa: ouch EU jump gets big. is that pure paging effect?
Maria: largely. A100 region had higher paging pressure and less effective fused kernels for our quantized path. paging spikes correlated with >1s disk queues in the iostats.
Dmitri: did you try adaptive prefetch based on recent hit streak?
Maria: yes. adaptive policy: base p=0.2, increase to 0.7 after 3+ consecutive hits. Results: hitrate ~0.73 (close to static 0.6) but p99(us-east)=98ms, p99(eu-west)=152ms. So adaptive saved p99 while keeping hitrate high.
Ajay: what about concurrency scaling? numbers at 8-concurrency?
Maria: those numbers are at concurrency=8. At concurrency=1 p99 delta between configs was smaller (~10-15ms). High concurrency amplifies the cost of mis-prefetching because it increases paging overlap.
Kevin: kernel breakdown? any kernel choice sensitivity?
Maria: H100: fused attention kernel + kv-cache hotpath gives ~10% lower p99 when hitrate>0.7. A100: our int8 quant path used a different matmul kernel that had higher tail variance; under paging it amplified p99.
Lisa: can you drop the exact command/config?
Maria: ```bash
./bench --trace traces/10k-mix.json \
  --gpu h100 --region us-east \
  --prefetch-strategy hybrid --prefetch-prob 0.3 \
  --adaptive-streak-threshold 3 \
  --evict-window-s=300 \
  --concurrency 8
```
Dmitri: did you try changing KV bucket size? more memory -> less paging?
Maria: quick sweep: 4GB buckets vs 8GB. 8GB improves hitrate ~+0.03 and reduces eu-west p99 by ~12-18ms for static-prefetch configs. Cost increases though.
ci-bot: Perf-run completed: run_id=2026-03-15_14-32, artifact=https://ci.internal/runs/2026-03-15_14-32
Maria: plan: run longer 100k trace, test hybrid-adaptive (start low p, raise aggressively on streak), and include kernel toggles (fused vs generic) in the matrix. also simulate fallback-to-smaller-model when p99>150ms.
Kevin: +1. let's also test with a realistic bursty seqlen tail (simulate 2% super-long sessions) — those may blow up paging.
Ajay: sounds good. if adaptive keeps p99 reasonable it'd be a good candidate for dedicated pool rollout (lower cost than full static-prefetch). :thumbsup:
Maria: agreed — I'll queue the long-run matrix and post results tomorrow.
